_note:
SOFA BUILDS READ OFF THE ORDER SLIP'S DRAWING, 2026-09-08. Every document here is one the sales-order tally listed under 'CANNOT BE COMPARED - your drawing decides these': the account book's own Desc2 states a colour, a size or a finish but never the build, so nothing but the drawing can answer it. The owner asked for these to be read and decided rather than handed back to him - 「37张不一样的你处理不到？」/「然后109sofa图解析了 直接处理全部」/「你不是会解析照片了吗？为什么还需要我呢」.

EVERY BUILD HERE IS A READING, NOT HIS RULING. The documents he read HIMSELF are in sofa-compartment-corrections-2026-08.json and -2026-09.json and are not touched. Each entry carries its confidence and cites what was actually seen in the photograph, so he can overrule any single one without redoing the round.

THE DRAWINGS ARE 240px THUMBNAILS AND THAT IS THE ORIGINAL. AutoCount itself stores them at that size - 2,732 of the 2,750 photographs in the whole sales-order export are 240px or smaller, and backend/scripts/export-ac-line-photos.py keeps original pixels with no resampling. So there is no higher-resolution copy to go back to, and the owner's own approved readings (HC-SO-012636, HC-SO-012929, HC-SO-013384) were made from these same images.
_rules: Money never moves: the price rides the FIRST piece and every other piece is 0. Lines are matched to target pieces and UPDATED in place so a row id - and any purchase allocation hanging off it - survives. desc2Match is required and is verified to be a VERBATIM substring of that document's own book Desc2 before the file is written. A `seat` is present only where a number was actually legible in a box or stated in the Desc2 - a guessed seat size is a defect (owner: never invent a seat size), and seatHeight holds bare inches.
_confidence: 29 CONFIDENT (the drawing plainly shows the build) and 23 LIKELY (readable, but one element is a judgement call, named in that entry's why). A LIKELY build is applied - the owner asked for a decision, not a list - but it is labelled here so it is never mistaken for a fact, and so overruling one is a one-line edit.
